title: Beyond Belief: Evaluating and Mitigating LLM Susceptibility to Misinformation
abstract: arXiv:2610.33962v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Tool-using large language models (LLMs) must decide whether external information warrants action. We investigate whether their expressed credibility judgments reliably indicate behavioral resistance to misinformation. We evaluate five LLMs on 196 constructed false notices paired with legitimate counterparts and 204 archived attacks adapted to simulated tool use. When asked to act on the constructed notices, models issue harmful tool calls in 27%--99% of cases they have rated untrustworthy. Removing the preliminary rating step increases harmful execution by 15 percentage points on average, showing that credibility elicitation itself changes the behavior being evaluated. Interventions that improve credibility discrimination do not consistently yield safer actions. translated_title: 超越信念：评估与缓解大语言模型对错误信息的易感性
translated_abstract: 使用工具的大语言模型（LLM）必须判断外部信息是否值得采取行动。我们研究了它们所表达的可信度判断是否能可靠地反映其对错误信息的行为抵抗能力。我们在196条构建的虚假通知（配有对应的合法通知）以及204条适配模拟工具使用的存档攻击上评估了五个大语言模型。当被要求对构建的虚假通知采取行动时，模型在它们已评定为不可信的案例中，有27%至99%的情况发出了有害的工具调用。移除预先评分这一步骤会使有害执行平均增加15个百分点，这表明可信度引出本身就会改变被评估的行为。旨在提升可信度辨别能力的干预措施并不总能带来更安全的行为。简单的预先警告在五个模型中的四个里显著减少了有害执行，但在主要评估中，两种经过测试的生成示例预反驳方法均未能超越其效果。（原文摘要至此截断）
tldr: 该研究发现大语言模型口头表达的可信度判断并不能可靠地转化为对错误信息的行为抵抗——即使模型已将信息评定为不可信，仍有27%至99%的情况会执行有害的工具调用，而简单的预先警告是缓解这一问题的有效手段。
en_tdlr: This study finds that LLMs' expressed credibility judgments do not reliably translate into behavioral resistance to misinformation—models issue harmful tool calls in 27%–99% of cases they rated untrustworthy, and a simple forewarning proves an effective mitigation strategy.
